derivation: Derived GEOMETRICALLY from the real TY2025 f1040.pdf (IRS fillable form), not from field-name numbering: for every entry, the widget /Rect of the field (read with pypdf) was matched against the printed line labels extracted with `pdftotext -bbox` on the blank form; a field is assigned to the line whose printed label sits on the same row (widget y-center within ~6pt of the label row). The spikes/pdf-fill/targets.json hints were treated as unverified and several proved wrong (e.g. its second candidate set points line 11/15 at dependents-table fields f1_39/f1_43). TY2025 numbering notes: the form prints AGI as line 11a (page 1) repeated as 11b (page 2); the standard-deduction amount box is line 12e (12a-12d are claim/checkbox items); the capital gain line is printed as 7a. Engine line numbers follow the engine's own numbering (7, 11, 12), so `source_line` records which engine line feeds each form field when they differ. Dependents table (page 1): the printed table is TRANSPOSED — dependents run across the columns (printed 'Dependent 1'..'Dependent 4' headers centered over the four field columns at x 145-251 / 253-359 / 361-467 / 469-576) and the questions run down the rows: (1) First name = Table_Dependents Row1 (f1_31..f1_34), (2) Last name = Row2 (f1_35..f1_38), (3) SSN = Row3 (f1_39..f1_42), (4) Relationship = Row4 (f1_43..f1_46) — row assignments verified by matching each field row's y-center (477/465/453/441) to the printed (1)-(4) label rows from pdftotext -bbox. Question (7) 'Child tax credit / Credit for other dependents' is Row7: TWO sibling Btn fields per dependent — c1_28[0]/c1_29[0]/c1_30[0]/c1_31[0] whose single widget sits in the LEFT sub-column (x 148/256/364/472, under the printed 'Child tax credit' sub-header) with on-state /1, and c1_28[1]/c1_29[1]/c1_30[1]/c1_31[1] whose widget sits in the RIGHT sub-column (x 198/306/414/522, under 'Credit for other dependents') with on-state /2 (field structure and widget /AP /N keys read with pypdf; all eight fields verified). Filling the wrong sibling is exactly the failure the audited fill catches (the [0] field has no /2 state).
